quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CEO/CFO): revenue of $103 million, down 13% from the prior quarter, with non-GAAP earnings of $0.23 per share, largely in line with expectations. On a sell-through basis sales were down only 3% sequentially, as sell-through exceeded sell-in and channel inventory built in Q3 was worked down. Revenue mix was 37% industrial, 34% consumer, 15% communications and 14% computer, less favorable than the gross-margin guidance assumed, so non-GAAP gross margin came in slightly below the range at 53.3%; non-GAAP operating expenses of $45 million came in well below the $47 million outlook. Quarterly cash flow from operations was $26 million and CapEx $7 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $103 million (down 13% QoQ); non-GAAP EPS $0.23; non-GAAP gross margin 53.3%; non-GAAP opex $45 million vs $47 million outlook

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2025 (CEO/CFO): the company returned to growth, with revenue up 6% and 3 of the 4 end-market categories up year-over-year. Non-GAAP gross margin was 55.1%, up 70 basis points, mainly on a higher industrial mix plus higher back-end manufacturing volumes; non-GAAP OpEx rose 5% and non-GAAP operating margin rose 100 basis points to 13.9%; non-GAAP EPS of $1.25 was up 8%. Cash flow from operations was $112 million (up $30 million), CapEx $24 million and free cash flow $87 million; $145 million (167% of free cash flow) was returned via buybacks and dividends. Revenue outside cell phone applications has averaged 12% growth over the past 2 years.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue up 6%; non-GAAP gross margin 55.1%; non-GAAP operating margin 13.9%; non-GAAP EPS $1.25 (up 8%); free cash flow $87 million; $145 million returned to shareholders

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 outlook (CFO): revenue between $104 million and $109 million; non-GAAP gross margin between 53% and 54% on a more favorable mix (higher industrial and consumer share); non-GAAP operating expenses of $46 million, plus or minus $0.5 million; GAAP results to include a restructuring charge of between $3.5 million and $4 million; effective tax rate of 7% to 8% for the quarter and the year (solar credits are nonrecurring and the tax rate on foreign earnings rises). For 2026 the company is planning for growth similar to 2025 year-over-year and will be cautious with investments until bookings step up; industrial is expected to be the fastest-growing market again, starting with a strong Q1, and consumer to grow sequentially in Q1.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue between $104 million and $109 million; non-GAAP gross margin between 53% and 54%; non-GAAP opex $46 million plus or minus $0.5 million; tax rate 7% to 8%

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and inventory (CEO/CFO): bookings improved significantly in Q4 after slowing in the prior quarter, partly because excess appliance inventory shipped into the U.S. ahead of the tariffs was absorbed (the largest U.S. appliance OEM, not named, reported that the preloaded inventory has largely dissipated); industrial was a key driver of the bookings uptick. Appliance demand still faces headwinds (low U.S. existing home sales, the tariff effect on appliance prices, soft China housing), so management stays conservative on consumer. Channel inventory fell by about half a week to 9.4 weeks in Q4 and is to be brought back to a healthier level; balance-sheet inventories rose by $2 million and days of inventory on hand rose to 313 on the lower revenue, while wafer inventory came down in 2025 and inventory days are expected to fall over the course of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: channel inventory 9.4 weeks (down about half a week); days of inventory on hand 313

quarterly_data.signal: End markets Q4 2025 (CFO): industrial revenue down 23% sequentially after 2 very strong quarters, reflecting seasonality and variable order patterns, but up 15% for 2025; consumer (predominantly appliances) down 13% sequentially on the overhang of appliance inventory shipped into the U.S. ahead of tariffs, down more than 15% half-over-half, yet slightly up for the year; computer down 5% on lower tablet revenue partly offset by notebooks (down 2% for the year); communications up 15% sequentially on new cell phone design ramps and the India 5G broadband business (up 6% for the year).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 industrial down 23% QoQ (2025 up 15%); consumer down 13% QoQ; computer down 5%; communications up 15% QoQ (2025 up 6%)

quarterly_data.signal: High-power and industrial (CEO): industrial revenue grew 15% in 2025 on electrification, renewable energy and grid modernization. The high-power industrial business had a record year with double-digit growth, driven by electric rail (a very strong position in the India locomotive market) and high-voltage DC transmission projects delivering renewable energy to the grid; recent design wins are expected to drive continued high-power growth in 2026 and beyond. Q4 wins included a leading European maker of inverters for utility-scale solar and battery storage (not named), commuter trains and street cars in Europe and Africa, and multiple power-grid projects in India. Metering grew double digits on smart-meter deployments in India and Japan, with customers migrating to the 900 and 1,250-volt GaN products for protection against India grid voltage swings; power tools also grew.
quarterly_data.figure: industrial revenue grew 15% in 2025; high-power business record year with double-digit growth

quarterly_data.signal: PowiGaN and product pipeline (CEO): revenue from PowiGaN products grew more than 40% in 2025 and GaN is 'pretty meaningful today'; design win value grew 10% in 2025, with particular strength in GaN and high-power products. Q4 GaN design wins included a dual USB-C charging port (charging ports integrated with AC outlets were called an ideal application for its integrated GaN solutions). The new TinySwitch-5 ICs have a healthy pipeline of designs scheduled to begin production in the second half of 2026, and the multi-output GaN-based InnoMux-2 ICs are seeing strong design traction in TVs. Investment priorities are shifting toward AI data center, industrial and automotive, with the R&D pipeline streamlined for faster time to market.
quarterly_data.figure: PowiGaN revenue grew more than 40% in 2025; design win value up 10% in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: AI data center (CEO): in Q4 production began on a new server auxiliary power design for a U.S. cloud services provider (not named) using a GaN-based InnoSwitch, described as 'an important validation of the latest products that we have'. Auxiliary power is a key aspect of engagements with data-center customers, including NVIDIA's next-gen 800-volt DC architecture, where the 1,700-volt GaN solutions offer 'a compelling alternative to silicon carbide'. Aux power is only a small part of the system and serves as an entry socket; the company is looking to intersect the main power supplies, a much more significant SAM, which is in development now. Data center is the longest-term play and will not be material for a couple of years.
quarterly_data.figure: server aux design in production at a U.S. cloud services provider; 1,700-volt GaN for 800-volt DC; not material for a couple of years

quarterly_data.signal: Automotive (CEO/CFO): steady progress in EVs with auto-qualified InnoSwitch products for inverter emergency power supplies: a Q4 design win at a top Chinese Tier 1 supplying a leading EV maker, and production began the week of the call on a design at the #1 European EV carmaker (neither named). The EV market is slower than hoped and some design ramps have pushed out. Asked whether auto could reach an analyst-cited low tens of millions of revenue this year or is more of a 2027 target, the CEO said the latter is fair and the CFO put the window at 12 months or 18 months.
quarterly_data.figure: auto revenue ramp window of 12 months or 18 months (analyst's revenue level not restated by management)

quarterly_data.signal: Cost actions and leadership (CEO/CFO): non-GAAP expenses were cut by more than $2 million from the prior quarter in Q4, and a restructuring carried out the week of the call reduced the global workforce by about 7% to align expenses with revenue and free up investment in products, people and markets. Asked whether OpEx would come down by a few more million dollars in the June quarter, the CFO answered 'for the year ... call it, $3 million to $5 million range' (what the range measures was not spelled out) and said the aim is to bring OpEx growth to about half of revenue growth, while reviewing all programs and the go-to-market vs R&D and G&A mix. New team members: Nancy Erba as CFO (joined a month before the call), Chris Jacobs from Micron Technology heading Marketing and Product Strategy, and Julie Currie as Head of People and Culture Transformation; Jen Lloyd is in her first 6 months as CEO.
quarterly_data.figure: global workforce reduced by about 7%; Q4 non-GAAP expenses down more than $2 million QoQ; for the year OpEx 'call it, $3 million to $5 million range' (CFO)

contracts.signal: Auxiliary power is a key aspect of Power Integrations' data-center engagements, including with NVIDIA on its next-gen 800-volt DC architecture, where Power Integrations' 1,700-volt GaN solutions offer 'a compelling alternative to silicon carbide'. The CEO cited the NVIDIA work as an example of the reorganization: 'We've got much more openness in terms of our road maps and our product development discussions', with focus areas pivoted to intersect the customer's needs.
